findings.title: Omitting period_end_to still skips the newer-direction refetch
findings.evidence: service.py _needs_fetch end_of_data branch gates the newer check on `want_to is not None`; with want_to=None (upper bound omitted) no refetch happens even when fetched_to is bounded. Reviewer run (wikiR3, full end_of_data store + fixture root whose consistent lrb history adds 2026-09-30): request without period_end_to -> 0 HTTP, complete, 36 periods, last=2026-06-30 while the provider serves 2026-09-30; the explicit to=2026-12-31 control refetches to 37 periods and then repeats at 0 HTTP.
findings.recommendation: Treat want_to=None as unbounded: refetch when fetched_to is not None (open upper edge never verified), or return partial with a named gap; add a no-to regression.

findings.evidence: Crafted token fsv-...:5 on a three-statement request: income resumes correctly (first report 72 rows, min ordinal 6) while balance_sheet returns its full 33 periods and cash_flow its full 36 (was complete/0-reports). reuse_only+continuation now rejected: CWP CLI exit 2 request_error (contracts.py:205-207) and FF exit 2 request_error (ff_financial_statements.py:78-81).
